overview: This Senate resolution supports naming May 2026 "National Foster Care Month" and May 31, 2026, "National Foster Parent Appreciation Day." Foster care is the system that temporarily places children with relatives or other caregivers when they can't safely live with their parents. The resolution describes challenges children face, such as long stays, frequent moves and school changes, and young people aging out at 18 or older without a permanent family, and it notes that placements with relatives tend to be more stable. It encourages Congress to adopt policies that support struggling families, prevent children from entering foster care, reunite families or promote adoption when appropriate, and help youth transition to adulthood. It is symbolic and does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 14, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to the hardships children in foster care face and honors the foster parents and workers who support them.
against: Critics say the resolution only encourages Congress to act and does not itself change any foster care law, program, or funding.
